subject: Ty Mawr/ Great House, Llandough, Cardiff
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Dear Rhodri, dear colleagues,
>
> Diolch am eich cydnabyddiaeth ar 8 Medi. On the Welsh Language Standards
point raised in your signature — I am Welsh and I would be glad to receive
correspondence in Welsh, but please use whichever language is quicker for
you. I do not want language to delay anything, and I will not treat a Welsh
reply as needing translation.
>
> This is a request under section 1 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000
and, so far as the records concern the historic environment, under the
Environmental Information Regulations 2004.
>
> **First, a point of housekeeping. Nothing in this email amends,
clarifies, narrows or withdraws my requests of 8, 15 or 17 September.**
Those stand exactly as made and their statutory periods run from their own
dates. This is an additional request, and I would not want it to be treated
as restarting any clock. On my reckoning:
>
> - **8 September 2026** — FOI/EIR on R. F. Suggett's December 1988
unpublished records, H. J. Thomas's 1974 survey, the source of the "held by
the National Museum of Wales" attribution, and copy correspondence with
Amgueddfa Cymru, GGAT, Cadw and the Vale. Acknowledged by you the same day,
twenty working days. **Due Tuesday 6 October 2026.** No reference number
issued; nothing yet supplied.
> - **15 September 2026** — catalogue check on Emergency Recording case
**RCS2/1/1777**, filed under Great House (Ty Mawr), Bonvilston, where the
material described is the pattern one would expect for the Llandough
demolition. **Due Tuesday 13 October 2026.**
> - **17 September 2026** — whether the Commission was notified, consulted
or asked to record the farmhouse before its demolition on 6 December 1988.
**Due Thursday 15 October 2026.**
>
> The second and third received only the automated enquiry acknowledgement,
which cites fifteen working days and notes that the priority search service
is suspended. I understand the staffing position and I am not complaining
about it. But both emails ask for recorded information, and a request for
recorded information is a request under section 1 whether or not it is
labelled as one. **Please confirm that all three are logged as FOIA / EIR
requests and let me have the reference numbers.** If they are currently
sitting in the research-enquiry queue rather than the information-rights
queue, that is easily fixed now and much harder to fix later.
>
> **On the number of requests.** I am conscious that this is my fifth email
in twelve days. It is not an attempt to burden the Commission. Each request
arose from a document I only found after sending the last one — the GGAT
1990 assessment led me to Suggett, Suggett's own note led me to the lost
correspondence, and a Coflein search led me to RCS2/1/1777. I am content
for all of them to be answered together in a single response if that is
more efficient for you, and if the whole exceeds the appropriate limit
under section 12 I will happily tell you which items to do first rather
than have anything refused outright. Please just ask.
>
> **The site.** Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (Llandochau) juxta
Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan — the community of St Dochdwy's Church and
Llandough Hospital. **Not** Llandough near Cowbridge, and **not** Ty Mawr,
Bonvilston (Cadw 13603), which is a different and still-standing house.
NPRN 20182. ST 1681 7331. HER GGAT02038s. Now Church View Close.
Outbuildings demolished 30 November 1988; farmhouse 6 December 1988.
>
> Holdings I am aware of include file references **NA/GL/88/49** and
**NA/GL/89/208**, NMR site file material catalogued on Coflein (a plan with
additions dated 12 December 1988, a descriptive account, a press cutting),
Inventory working papers for Glamorgan Inventory site 425, and the disputed
ERC bundle RCS2/1/1777.
>
> **Why this matters to me.** The farm was my family's. The immediate
reason for this request is a line in your own records: R. F. Suggett's
December 1988 assessment notes that *"Correspondence between C. N. Johns
and Mrs Buckler, Great House Farm, has been lost from the file since
1986/87"*, and that *"There is apparently no photographic record of the
site."* Mrs Buckler was my relative. I want the correspondence if it
survives, the record of how it came to be lost if it does not, and the rest
of the file either way. I am not asking the Commission for a view on title
or on the legality of the demolition, and I would not expect one.
>
> **Information requested**
>
> Please supply copies, so far as held:
>
> 1. A full contents list or file schedule for **NA/GL/88/49** and
**NA/GL/89/208**, itemising every document on each file, whether or not the
documents themselves are disclosed.
> 2. Copies of all documents on those two files.
> 3. **The file cover, front sheet or wrapper of each file**, and any
enclosure list, loans register, issue slip, reader-request record or
file-tracking entry attached to or kept for them.
> 4. Every record concerning the **C. N. Johns / Mrs Buckler
correspondence** recorded as lost since 1986/87: any surviving copy, draft,
extract, summary, index entry or catalogue stub; any contemporaneous or
later note of its loss; any record of a search for it; any record of who
consulted, borrowed or handled the file between 1 January 1985 and 31
December 1988; and any internal or external correspondence about its
absence. If no such record exists, please say so expressly rather than
leaving it unaddressed.
> 5. The Commission's **retention and disposal schedule** applicable to
site files and correspondence files in the 1980s and today, and
confirmation whether any records relating to this site have been destroyed
under it, and if so when and under what authority.
> 6. Whether the files listed above have been **reviewed for transfer to,
or retention from, The National Archives or the Glamorgan Archives**, and
the outcome of any such review.
> 7. All **Inventory working papers, drafts, card-index entries and record
cards** for the site, including those for Glamorgan Inventory site 425.
> 8. All **photographs** of the site in any format — prints, negatives,
transparencies, digital images, and any oblique or vertical aerial coverage
of Llandough showing the farm at any date — whether or not catalogued, with
their catalogue entries. Given Suggett's 1988 note that there is apparently
no photographic record, **please state expressly whether the Commission
holds none**, and whether any images sit within RCS2/1/1777 or in
uncatalogued Emergency Recording material.
> 9. Confirmation, from the location plan, map copies and photographs
inside **RCS2/1/1777**, whether that bundle is Bonvilston or Llandough. If
Llandough, please re-link it to NPRN 20182 and supply a contents list and
copies. Please also check adjacent case **RCS2/1/1776**. *(This is my
request of 15 September, restated here for completeness only — it stands on
its own date.)*
> 10. Any record of a site visit, watching brief, recording exercise or
emergency recording carried out or considered before, during or after the
demolition; any notification of the proposed demolition, from whom and on
what date; and any decision **not** to record the building together with
the reasons recorded for it. The building was not listed — Cadw inspected
on 29 July 1988 and did not list it — so I make no assumption that the
Commission was entitled to notice. What I would like to know is what the
Commission's own criteria for initiating Emergency Recording were at the
time, and whether this site was considered against them. Contemporary
reports of 3 December 1988 stated that Cadw was considering emergency
listing and that discussion with the Commission was being arranged. The
house came down three days later.
> 11. The **1974 survey by H. J. Thomas**, his site notes of 26 April 1974
and 12 December 1988, and any measured drawings, sketches, plans or
elevations, published or unpublished.
> 12. **R. F. Suggett's December 1988 records in full** — every page, card,
continuation sheet, annotation and enclosure — not only the passages
concerning the c.1880 find.
> 13. Any record of the source of the statement that the c.1880 ironwork
"is held by the National Museum of Wales", and any later file that
confirms, corrects or withdraws that attribution.
> 14. All correspondence between the Commission and any of the following
concerning this site, 1970–1995: Cadw or the Welsh Office; the
Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust; Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council; BP
Properties Limited or its agents, including Debenham Tewson & Chinnocks;
Persimmon Homes (Wales) Limited; Ideal Homes Wales Limited; Amgueddfa
Cymru; any Member of Parliament; and any member of my family.
> 15. Any accession records for material deposited with the Commission by
GGAT, Cadw, Cotswold Archaeology or any other body relating to this site.
>
> **Practicalities.** Please reply by email to this address. I cannot
attend in person and I am not seeking anything that attracts a charge.
Scans are fine. Where an item is already on Coflein, a stable reference and
link is enough **provided** you confirm the online record is complete. If
any item is held elsewhere — The National Archives, Glamorgan Archives,
Cadw, Heneb or Amgueddfa Cymru — please name the body and reference so I
can apply there directly, which I will.
>
> Finally, so that it is on record from the outset rather than raised
later: please let me have the name and contact details of the officer
responsible for information rights at the Commission, and confirmation of
the internal review procedure, so that I know where to direct any review
request if one becomes necessary.
>
> With thanks for your patience with a long list.
>
> Yn gywir / Yours faithfully,
>
> Sion Buckler
> [email redacted]
